# Incident Report: MTA 2026-02-28 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.2.28.88 |
| MAC | 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR |
| Logged-in domain user | brolf (confirmed via Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges between 10.2.28.88 and DC at 10.2.28.2) |
| Domain | easyas123.tech (DC: EASYAS123-DC.easyas123.tech) |

MAC-to-IP binding confirmed via ARP (10.2.28.88 ↔ 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad); DHCP request for the same MAC also carries hostname DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR. LAN gateway/DC is 10.2.28.2 (NBNS name EASYAS123).

## Malware Family
**NetSupport RAT** (commercial NetSupport Manager remote-control software abused as a RAT). Attribution is **behavioral, not IDS-signature-confirmed** (no IDS/alert export was provided with this evidence set) — but the evidence is unambiguous protocol-level confirmation, not inference: the client sends `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` and the remote server responds `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.92 (Windows NT)`, with the exact NetSupport client-control command grammar (`CMD=POLL`, `CMD=ENCD`, `ES=1`, `DATA=<encrypted blob>`) observed in the reassembled TCP stream.

No delivery/dropper chain is visible in this capture — the C2 beacon (DNS lookup for the C2 domain, first POST to the C2) begins at t≈44.7s, essentially at the start of the capture, indicating the host was already infected before packet capture began. Only post-compromise C2 traffic is present.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint (grounded in traffic):**
- `45.131.214.85:443` — TCP/HTTP (plaintext, not TLS, despite port 443), stream index 40, source port 51912 on victim. Sustained beaconing for the entire capture duration (~15,637s / ~4.3 hours), with dozens of `POST /fakeurl.htm` requests.

**Malicious domain:**
- `vadusa.xyz` — resolved by 10.2.28.88 via internal DNS (10.2.28.2) to 45.131.214.85 at capture time 44.888646s.

**Malicious URL:**
- `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm` — the sole C2 URI, hit repeatedly for the entire session with NetSupport RAT control-channel POST bodies (`CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD`, encrypted `DATA=` payloads).

**Transferred files / hashes:**
- None recoverable. The C2 channel payloads are encrypted (`DATA=` blobs), so no plaintext file transfer or hash could be extracted from this stream. All objects recoverable via `tshark --export-objects http` (Microsoft Delivery Optimization content, Windows Update `.cab` files, etc.) are benign OS/background traffic, not malware artifacts.

**Benign context (not indicators):** the DNS lookup for `www.fmcsa.dot.gov` at t≈44.4s, immediately adjacent to the `vadusa.xyz` lookup, is a legitimate US government site (Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration) resolved to Akamai IP 23.64.147.24 — likely an open browser tab/decoy page, not malicious infrastructure, and carries no indicators itself. All Microsoft, Adobe, Bing, MSN, Office, Skype, Windows Update, and NVIDIA traffic in the capture is standard Windows/enterprise background telemetry and is excluded from the IOC list.

## Summary
Host DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR (10.2.28.88, MAC 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad), logged in as domain user **brolf**, is compromised with **NetSupport RAT**, beaconing continuously to **vadusa.xyz (45.131.214.85:443)** via `POST /fakeurl.htm` for the full duration of the capture. Recommend isolating the host, blocking 45.131.214.85 and vadusa.xyz at the perimeter, and resetting brolf's domain credentials.
